tolerance.comparison_method: Open CASCADE re-import; compare axis-aligned bounding box, solid count, and volume. Normative standard dimensions are the primary acceptance criterion; vendor STEP files are secondary geometric oracles.

external_references.standard: catalog record: module 2.0, 20 teeth, width 16, bore 8
external_references.notes: The reference is a blank tip-diameter envelope. The parametric envelope matches it exactly: tip diameter 44 mm, face width 16 mm, bore 8 mm, and volume 23524.2 mm3. No tooth form is claimed for this reference.

Detailed reference: nominal-diameter shank, a 45-degree countersink with a 22.5-degree conical top-edge break (0.05 mm inset), and a conical socket (45-degree rim over a hexagon at the nominal 2.0 mm across flats, 70-degree drill point). The reference socket reaches the head underside at the hex corners and its drill point enters the shank, deeper than ISO 10642's nominal t = 1.2 mm; the deeper reference socket is modeled and recorded. Volume 96.478 vs 96.488 mm3 (0.01%).

Detailed nut: a true conical washer face on each bearing face (60 degrees) trimmed by the six flats, plus the reference bore lead-in. The across-flats is checked from the face-circle vertex ring, because OCCT's Bnd_Box includes the untrimmed conical surfaces and cannot confirm s. The golden M5 uses the old DIN 934 height 4.0 mm against ISO 4032's 4.7 mm; the standard value is modeled.
DIN 125 A M3 dimensions (d1 3.2, d2 7, h 0.5) match the golden and ISO 7089; the golden is a standard-correct plain washer.

DIN 125 A M8: d1 8.4, d2 16, h nominal 1.6 mm (limits 1.4..1.8). The reference is 1.8 mm, the ISO 7089 h_max, so the reference thickness is chosen at h_max to reproduce the golden within the standard.

DIN 127 B M4: d1 4.1, d2 7.6, s 0.9, h 1.8. The downloaded reference has four B-spline side surfaces and two planar caps (6 faces, 12 edges, 8 vertices) and a parallel-plane split at the +X side. The parametric part uses the same native topology and reproduces the reference's eight split-cap vertices exactly (corner endpoint overrides from the reference), with smooth cubic B-spline sides. Volume 27.43 vs 27.64 mm3; exact tessellated bbox 7.603 x 7.636 x 1.751 mm. The golden's exact bbox is 7.592 x 7.600 x 1.751 mm; OCCT Bnd_Box reports the looser 9.915 x 11.120 x 1.773 mm control hull for the golden's high-degree surfaces. DIN side length b = 1.5; the radial section width is (d2 - d1) / 2 = 1.75 mm.

external_references.family: hexagon socket set screw with flat point
external_references.notes: DIN 913 M3 x 5: d 3, socket s 1.5 (upper limit 1.545), socket depth t 2.0, 90-degree point cone; the downloaded reference uses a 2.2 mm point flat, so the parametric part matches that reference value (DIN d_p max is 2.0), which places the cone end at z = 0.4 and makes the Z=0..1 cross-sections coincide. The reference's socket across flats 1.5588 is above the DIN max 1.545, so the socket uses the standard limit; that accounts for the remaining volume difference (30.522 vs 30.447 mm3). external_references.manufacturer: MakerBeam AS drawing; reference regenerated from the MIT pythonparts model
external_references.notes: The reference STEP is regenerated locally with CadQuery from the MIT pythonparts MakerBeam model (part.py), which encodes the section of MakerBeam drawing article 100168 (DXF geometry and printed dimensions). It is an independent implementation reference, not a manufacturer STEP file: the MakerBeam technical-drawing folder is access-restricted. Both models use the sharp dimensioned outline; MakerBeam's R0.2 corner and edge radii and the M3 end threads are omitted. Bounding box, volume, face counts, and the 1.25 mm bore cylinder match exactly. The step.parts MakerBeam model was measured and rejected: its section area is 37.7 mm2 and its X-shaped struts contradict the drawing's 4 x 4 core and 48.75 mm2 area.

review.reason: owner reported 'look perfect' after the shared-frame visual comparison

external_references.designation: Rigid sleeve coupling OD 15 / bore 5 x 20
external_references.notes: The catalogue labels this file a beam coupling, but it is a plain tube: OD 15, bore 5, length 20, with 2 cylinders and 2 planes. It is used only as a plain rigid-sleeve envelope reference and is not treated as a beam-coupling model. The parametric rigid coupling has the same volume (3141.59 mm3), the same 2 cylinder + 2 plane inventory, and bore/outer radii 2.5/7.5 mm. The generation recipe uses --goldenFrame so the comparison output matches the reference's X-long, origin-centred frame; the rigid_coupling builder itself keeps the library Z-up, z = 0..length frame. No keyway, set screw, clamp slit, flexible element, or torque rating is present in either model.

external_references.manufacturer: FreeCAD-library model by nachotineo (CC BY 3.0); distributed by step.parts
external_references.notes: The reference is the FreeCAD-library DIN 471 A20 model (CC BY 3.0, by nachotineo), distributed by step.parts. Its free-state outline is the source of the parametric ring's outline; DIN 471 does not dimension the curve between the back and the lugs. The model's free bore is 18.6 mm against the DIN 471 d3 of 18.5 mm; the builder keeps the model outline and exposes the nominal d3 and groove d2 x m through the standard table and connectors. Bounding box, volume, and lug-hole/bore radii match. The reference writes 9 cylinders and the parametric model 16 because each long arc is split into two minor arcs for the extrusion compiler; the geometry is the same. The shaft groove is declared, not modelled. Sharp edges, no spring temper, no load rating. The generation recipe uses --goldenFrame so the comparison output matches the reference's YZ ring plane, +Y lugs, and x = s/2 near face; the din471_ring builder itself keeps the library XY-plane, z = 0..s frame.

external_references.notes: The reference is the CC0 Innerscene 8 mm set-screw shaft collar. Its file contains two solids: the collar body (volume 1150.77 mm^3) and a set screw (32.34 mm^3) whose thread is a large modeled helical surface. This library models the collar body with a clean radial hole and adds a DIN 916 M4 x 4 plain-envelope set screw (44.61 mm^3) placed coaxially in that hole; the thread is declared by connectors and never modelled, so the parametric set screw is a smooth envelope rather than the reference's thread. The recipe passes --thread M4 --drill 4.1 to reproduce the reference's measured 4.1 mm hole; the reference drill stops 0.07 mm inside the bore and leaves 4 planes, while the parametric hole opens cleanly into the bore. Totals: 2 solids, bbox 16 x 16 x 8 mm (the evaluated collar's hole-axis extent is 16.0075 from OCCT's boolean tolerance), volume 1194.24 vs 1183.11 mm^3 (0.94%), 5 cylinders + 4 cones + 12 planes. The evaluated compound is the primary artifact because the flat writer cannot trim the radial hole. No holding torque, material, or strength claim is made. Owner visual review verified 2026-11-13: reported 'absolutely beautiful - better than the golden'.

review.reason: owner reported 'absolutely beautiful - better than the golden' after the side-by-side comparison

external_references.standard: ISO 261 / ISO 68-1 (M6x1 thread interface); ISO 4762 (M6 x 16 clamp screw envelope)
external_references.notes: The reference is the CC0 Innerscene 20 mm clamp shaft collar. Its file contains two solids: the collar body (12955.59 mm^3) and an M6 x 16 clamp screw (761.28 mm^3) whose shank is a large modeled helical thread. The collar body is reproduced as a chamfered 40 x 20 x 15 annulus (0.2 mm rim chamfers) minus a real 0.8 mm radial slit opening at +Y, a modeled 6.1 mm clamp clearance passage along X at the measured 14.73 mm radial offset, and a 10.2 mm ISO 4762 head counterbore whose floor sits at x = 7.12. The parametric body is 12956.1 mm^3, within 0.5 mm^3 of the reference body, and its trimmed bbox is 40 x 39.996 x 15 mm (the slit removes the extreme +Y point, so the outside extent is sqrt(20^2 - 0.4^2) = 19.996). The example places a plain-envelope ISO 4762 M6 x 16 screw on the head seat (0.05 mm axial inset so it stays a separate solid, as in the reference); the thread is declared by connectors and never modelled, so the parametric screw is a smooth envelope at the ISO 68-1 external thread minor diameter (4.773 mm, the reference's thread root) rather than the reference's modeled helical thread. That keeps the shank visibly smaller than the 6.1 mm clearance hole, as in the reference, and gives a screw volume of 688.90 mm^3 vs the reference's 761.28 mm^3. Totals: 2 solids, volume 13645.00 vs 13716.88 mm^3 (0.52%), 10 cylinders + 8 cones + 15 planes. The evaluated compound restores the collar and screw layer colours through XCAF, so the clamp screw is visually distinct like the reference's material split. The evaluated compound is the primary artifact because the flat writer cannot trim the slit or the holes. No holding torque, material, or strength claim is made.

review.reason: owner reported 'looks perfect now' after the side-by-side comparison, including the corrected screw-envelope shank

external_references.designation: UCP204 pillow block bearing, 20 mm shaft
external_references.notes: The reference is the CC0 Innerscene UCP204 pillow block, an 8-solid assembly (housing 84287.6 mm^3, spherical-OD outer race 12160.1, extended inner race 13305.5, two seals 162.9 each, two DIN 916 M6 set screws 98.3 each, grease fitting 101.1; total 110376.6 mm^3). This library reproduces the same 8-part assembly. The housing is the base plate (127 x 38 x 16 mm, two 18 x 13 mm obround mounting slots on the 95 mm bolt pitch, 3.99 mm deep bottom centre relief, R3 corners) fused with the horseshoe arch (24 mm wide, r 31.7 mm crown, r 23.54 mm insert seat); the insert is a self-aligning outer race (spherical r 23.5 mm outside diameter, 34 mm bore, 16 mm wide), an extended inner race (31 mm outside diameter, 20 mm bore, 31 mm wide, 0.45 mm rim chamfers) with two 6.1 mm radial set-screw holes 120 degrees apart, two 1.1 mm contact seals, two DIN 916 M6 x 4 set screws, and a hex grease fitting on the crown. The parts sit at the reference's 0.025-0.05 mm clearances, so the OCCT-evaluated compound is 8 separate solids: bbox 127 x 38 x 70.35 mm, volume 110391.85 vs 110376.60 mm^3 (0.014%), 59 planes + 27 cylinders + 5 cones + 1 sphere. The parametric housing is 84306.3 vs the reference housing's 84287.6 mm^3 (0.02%); the outer race and seals match the reference exactly and the inner race is within 3 mm^3. Rolling elements and cage are omitted; the seat and shaft clearances are declared by connectors. The OCCT-evaluated compound is the primary artifact because the flat writer cannot trim the relief, seat bore, or set-screw holes. No load, life, or safety claim is made.
